description: Radxa ZERO 3E (Rockchip RK3566), 1 GB LPDDR4 (the user's SKU), microSD storage and no eMMC, Gigabit Ethernet and no Wi-Fi. A board record: Atlas flashes it from maskrom (rockusb) with Rockchip's loader file and no vendor tool; running, it serves the identity contract (board-lite, gaia/device.toml), read-only. Written from Radxa's docs, the Linux device tree and rkdeveloptool; untested on this board.

network.ethernet: Gigabit; PHY RTL8211F-CG (CNX product page); the device tree (rk3566-radxa-zero-3e.dts) gives PHY reset on GPIO3 PC0, active low
network.wifi_bt: none (the ZERO 3W has Wi-Fi 6 and Bluetooth 5.4; the 3E has neither)

ports: USB 2.0 Type-C OTG, which also takes the power input: the maskrom port

leds.name: green
leds.source: rk3566-radxa-zero-3.dtsi led-green (shared with the ZERO 3W's device tree)

camera.connectors: one 4-lane MIPI CSI connector, 22-pin, 0.5 mm pitch

storage_target_evidence: docs.radxa.com ZERO 3E page: microSD only, no eMMC (the ZERO 3W is the eMMC variant).
Atlas writes the SD card image from byte 0 (GPT, with u-boot-rockchip.bin at sector 64). Whether the RK3566's maskrom usbplug writes the SD card is UNCONFIRMED (todo).
instructions: Take out the microSD card and unplug the power.
Connect the board's USB 2.0 Type-C OTG port (the one that also takes the power) to this computer with a USB-A to USB-C cable. The green LED stays on in maskrom.
If the board has a MaskROM button, hold it while you connect the cable (UNCONFIRMED: see todo).
The board appears as 2207:350a (RK3566 maskrom). Atlas runs the loader's DDR init and usbplug, writes the image to the microSD card, reads it back and restarts the board.
todo: Sources: the maskrom steps, the OTG port and the green LED are from docs.radxa.com/en/zero/zero3/low-level-dev/install-os-on-emmc (fetched 2026-11-02). That page is the ZERO 3's eMMC guide; the 3E has no eMMC, so its SD steps are the same as the 3W's and need checking on the board. The PID 2207:350a is in rkdeveloptool 304f073's 99-rk-rockusb.rules line 18 (RK3566); lsusb on the board has the last word.
UNCONFIRMED: the MaskROM button. CNX lists one on the 3E; Radxa's page lists none. The instructions say to use it only if the board has one.

UNCONFIRMED: whether the RK3566's maskrom usbplug writes the microSD card at all. The record targets it through CHANGE_STORAGE id 2 (SD); Atlas reads READ_STORAGE back and refuses a mismatch, so a usbplug without SD support stops before writing.

2207:350a is shared by RK3566 and RK3568: any RK356x board in maskrom is offered as this record, and its loader reports the same chip family. Confirm with lsusb on the board, and add a second RK356x record only with a way to tell them apart.

The loader: rkbin f43a462's RKBOOT/RK3566MINIALL.ini (CHIP_NAME=RK3568) names rk3566_ddr_1056MHz_v1.23, rk356x_usbplug_v1.17 and rk356x_spl_v1.14 and builds rk356x_spl_loader_v1.23.114.bin with boot_merger. Those three parts are in fetch.lock (not in git). rkbin does not publish the merged loader, and no rk3566_loader_v*.bin exists in rkbin. Gaia needs: the merged rk356x_spl_loader_v*.bin, from a Gaia build; Gaia's ZERO 3W build is the closest source (not built yet, so no loader is on hand). ASK: does a Gaia build exist for the RK3566 ZERO 3E?

Gaia's facts (not verified on this side): sdcard.img is GPT with u-boot-rockchip.bin at 32 KiB (LBA 64), uboot-env at 16 MiB, then rootfs-a (extlinux), rootfs-b and data; mainline U-Boot 2026.01 and Linux 6.19; the gadget is usb0 at 10.55.0.1, the host gets 10.55.0.2.
UNCONFIRMED: the 40-pin header is populated on the 3E. UNCONFIRMED: a fan header (none found).
Network: Gigabit Ethernet (RTL8211F-CG); the Gaia image must bring the Ethernet up (DHCP on eth0 is UNCONFIRMED for this board) before board-lite answers.
